subject: mlt
lectureTitle: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
title: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
snippet: Explores the mathematical formulation of supervised regression, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), convex cost functions, the matrix derivation of the Normal Equation, and convergence properties of Batch Gradient Descent.

subject: mlt
lectureTitle: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
title: 1. Supervised Learning Formulation & Notations
snippet: Supervised regression learns a mapping function from input vectors to continuous target scalars by minimizing an empirical risk objective.

subject: mlt
lectureTitle: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
title: 2. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) Cost Surface
snippet: The squared error objective is strictly convex with respect to parameters, ensuring a unique global minimum when the design matrix is full rank.

subject: mlt
lectureTitle: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
title: 3. Step-by-Step Derivation of the Normal Equation
snippet: Setting the gradient of the matrix-vector residual sum of squares to zero yields the closed-form analytical solution.

subject: mlt
lectureTitle: Linear Regression, Loss Functions & Ordinary Least Squares
title: 4. Batch Gradient Descent & Hyperparameter Tuning
snippet: When matrix inversion is computationally prohibitive (O(d^3)), iterative first-order gradient descent scales efficiently to millions of features.

subject: mad2
title: History and Origins of JavaScript
snippet: Traces JavaScript from Java applets and Netscape (1995) through AJAX (2005) to ECMAScript and modern versions. Covers how its origins explain its quirks (silent failures, ambiguous syntax, limited I/O), its strengths (DOM, async), where it runs (browser, Node.js), how to run it, and useful references.

subject: mad2
title: 1. Java Applets and the Problem JavaScript Solved
snippet: Applets were isolated, powerful, but separate from the rest of the web page.

subject: mad2
title: 2. Netscape, the Glue Language, and the Name
snippet: JavaScript began in 1995 as a simple, forgiving glue language, not a language for large programs.

subject: mad2
title: 3. AJAX and the 2005 Turning Point
snippet: Fetching data in the background made web apps behave like desktop apps.

subject: mad2
title: 4. ECMAScript, ES Versions, and Feature Readiness
snippet: ECMAScript is the standard behind JavaScript, now released yearly and adopted feature by feature.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Supporting Old Browsers: Upgrade, Electron, Polyfills
snippet: Compilers and polyfills let modern code run on legacy browsers.

subject: mad2
title: 6. JavaScript Beyond the Browser
snippet: Node.js and Deno run JavaScript on the back end, but without the DOM.

subject: mad2
title: 7. Performance: Ease of Use First
snippet: Early JavaScript was slow by design priorities, but modern engines are fast.

subject: mad2
title: 8. Silent Failure and Strict Mode
snippet: JavaScript inherited HTML's forgiveness, which makes debugging hard; use strict mode.

subject: mad2
title: 9. Ambiguous Syntax, Semicolons, and Linters
snippet: Automatic semicolon insertion is vague, so always write semicolons and use a linter.

subject: mad2
title: 10. Limited Input/Output and the Console
snippet: The language has no direct way to talk to the user, so errors go to the console.

subject: mad2
title: 11. Strengths: DOM Integration and Asynchronous Processing
snippet: Direct DOM access plus the event loop make JavaScript suited to interactive apps.

subject: mad2
title: 12. How We Run JavaScript in This Course
snippet: On the front end, an HTML file loads the script, which needs a server and a browser.

subject: mad2
title: 13. The DOM as the Interaction Layer
snippet: The DOM lets JavaScript read input, change content and structure, and draw.

subject: mad2
title: 14. References and Utilities
snippet: Use a language reference, MDN, Babel, the browser console and Replit; be critical of tutorials.

subject: mad2
title: 15. Starter Example (Tutor Addition)
snippet: A minimal HTML plus JS project that shows script loading, the DOM, the console and a semicolon pitfall.

subject: mad2

title: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
snippet: A fast, Python-linked introduction to working JavaScript syntax: how front-end scripts are invoked from HTML, reserved words and literals, statements versus expressions, primitive data types, objects and functions as values, followed by a first Replit demo that prints to the console from script.js.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 1. Approach of This Part: Working Knowledge, Python as Anchor
snippet: Learn enough syntax to start, link it to Python, and learn the rest by programming.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 2. Front-End JavaScript Runs From an HTML Page
snippet: Without a document there is nothing useful for front-end JavaScript to do; the language is a loosely structured script.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 3. Identifiers and Reserved Words
snippet: Never use a reserved word, or a word you suspect is used by the language, as a variable name.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 4. Literals and Other Words to Avoid
snippet: true, false and null are literal values; avoid a few more words that are not strictly forbidden.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 5. Statements and Expressions
snippet: A statement is executed; an expression produces a value and can be used wherever a value is needed.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 6. Primitive Data Types
snippet: JavaScript has one number type, plus bigint, string and Boolean, and the non-values undefined and null.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 7. Objects and Functions as Values
snippet: Objects bundle data; functions can be stored in variables and inside objects.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 8. Demo: A Basic Replit Project
snippet: An HTML, CSS and JavaScript Repl gives index.html, script.js and style.css.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 9. Demo: Walking Through index.html
snippet: The script tag loads script.js; the rest is default Replit HTML plus a few added items.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 10. Demo: script.js, Run, Console and Shell
snippet: HTML output appears in the page pane; console.log output appears in the Console.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Syntax Basics: Statements, Expressions, Types, and a First Demo
title: 11. Syntax Demo (Tutor Addition)
snippet: A small tested script that shows each idea from this lecture.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
snippet: Covers JavaScript comments, identifiers and reserved words, Unicode and UTF-16, mixed-script variable names, scope with var, let and const, string basics and length, template strings, operator coercion, and loose versus strict equality.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 1. Comments, Identifiers and Reserved Words
snippet: JavaScript uses // for single-line and /* */ for multi-line comments, and reserved words like let cannot be used as identifiers.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 2. Unicode and UTF-16
snippet: Unicode assigns code points to characters, and most JavaScript engines represent them internally as UTF-16.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 3. Mixed-Script Variables
snippet: JavaScript accepts identifiers and string values in any script, but neutral Latin identifiers are the better convention.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 4. Scope: var, let and const
snippet: var leaks out of blocks, while let and const are block-scoped; prefer const, then let, and avoid var.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 5. String Basics
snippet: Strings have a length property, zero-based indexing and a substring method whose end index is excluded.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 6. String Length with Non-Latin Scripts
snippet: The length of a string depends on its internal representation, so it need not match the number of visible characters.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 7. Template Strings
snippet: Strings in backticks can interpolate any JavaScript expression written inside a dollar-brace placeholder.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 8. Operators and Type Coercion
snippet: JavaScript silently converts types around operators, so plus may join strings while star converts to numbers.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Basics: Comments, Unicode, Scope, Strings, Operators and Equality
title: 9. Equality: == versus ===
snippet: Double equals coerces types before comparing; triple equals does not, and is the safer default.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
snippet: Recaps strings, operators and equality, then covers undefined versus null, const and let semantics, conditions, for loops with for-in and for-of, other control-flow statements, the three function notations, IIFEs, and typeof with properties on functions.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 1. Recap: Strings, Operators and Equality
snippet: String length is predictable but depends on UTF-16, coercion is problematic, and strict equality is preferred.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 2. undefined versus null
snippet: undefined means no value has been given yet, while null is a value you explicitly set to mean nothing.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 3. let and const Revisited
snippet: const prevents reassigning the variable but does not freeze the contents of an object; let can be reassigned.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 4. Conditions
snippet: An if statement runs one branch or the other depending on a comparison.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 5. The C-style for Loop and const
snippet: A loop counter that is incremented with x++ must be declared with let, not const.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 6. for-in versus for-of
snippet: for-in gives the indices of an array, while for-of gives its values; for-of is the safer default.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 7. Other Control-Flow Statements
snippet: JavaScript also has while loops, break, continue and switch, similar to Python, C and Java.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 8. Function Notations
snippet: A function can be written as a declaration, a function expression assigned to a variable, or an arrow function.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 9. Immediately Invoked Function Expressions (IIFE)
snippet: An IIFE declares an anonymous function and invokes it at once, but it is no longer needed now that let and const exist.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript Control Flow, const vs let, and Function Notations
title: 10. typeof and Properties on Functions
snippet: Every function notation gives typeof equal to function, and functions can even hold properties, though this is best avoided.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
title: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
snippet: Transitions from basic console logging to frontend DOM manipulation, covering how to select and modify HTML elements, introduce time delays using async/await, and handle user inputs via event listeners.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
title: 1. From Console to DOM Manipulation
snippet: JavaScript in the browser is designed to manipulate the Document Object Model (DOM), moving beyond limited console.log debugging to actual user-facing interactions.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
title: 2. The Document Object and Element Selection
snippet: The global `document` variable provides methods like `getElementById` to hook into existing HTML elements and dynamically change their content.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
title: 3. UI Timing and Asynchronous Delays
snippet: Using `async` functions and `await new Promise` allows developers to pause JavaScript execution without freezing the browser, enabling timed UI updates.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Introduction to DOM Manipulation and Interactivity
title: 4. Event Listeners and Dynamic Styling
snippet: The `addEventListener` method binds user actions (like clicks) to anonymous arrow functions, allowing for dynamic updates to element content and CSS styles.

subject: mad2
title: Introduction to JavaScript Collections
snippet: Explores JavaScript collections starting with arrays as mixed-type lists. It introduces iterables, functional callbacks, modern data structures like Maps and Sets, array destructuring, and generators for cooperative concurrency.

subject: mad2
title: 1. Arrays as Generic Collections
snippet: Unlike C arrays, JavaScript arrays are generic, mixed-type collections (similar to Python lists) that can contain numbers, strings, and even functions simultaneously.

subject: mad2
title: 2. Iterables and Iteration
snippet: An iterable is an object accessed sequentially using a pointer (iterator). Examples include arrays, strings, maps, and the browser DOM tree.

subject: mad2
title: 3. First-Class Functions and Callbacks
snippet: JavaScript treats functions as first-class objects, allowing them to be passed as arguments (callbacks) to higher-order functions like map, filter, and find.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Maps, Sets, and Cleaner Syntax
snippet: Modern JavaScript introduced structures like Map, Set, WeakMap, and WeakSet to provide cleaner, more readable alternatives to old scoping hacks (like IIFEs).

subject: mad2
title: 5. Array Destructuring
snippet: Destructuring splits an array or object into multiple distinct variables, enabling Python-like named arguments and default values in JavaScript.

subject: mad2
title: 6. Generators and Cooperative Concurrency
snippet: Generators use the 'yield' keyword to pause execution and return a value without exiting, forming the basis for cooperative concurrency where multiple functions remain active.

subject: mad2
title: Screencast 2.1 - JavaScript - Basic Calculator
snippet: Builds a simple calculator with only HTML and JavaScript: a Bootstrap grid with a text box and a button, evaluating expressions with eval and math.js, reading and writing values through the DOM, validating input, catching errors, logging results by creating list items dynamically, and attaching events with addEventListener on body load.

subject: mad2
title: 1. Goal and Setup
snippet: The first version is a text box and a Calculate button that turns an expression such as 5 * 6 into 30, using only HTML and JavaScript.

subject: mad2
title: 2. Bootstrap Grid Layout
snippet: Linking Bootstrap CSS and JS and using a container with a row of three columns places the controls in the middle column.

subject: mad2
title: 3. Form Elements: Input and Button
snippet: A text input with id expression and a button with id calculate are the only controls needed.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Evaluating Strings with eval
snippet: eval takes an expression as a string, evaluates it at run time with correct operator order, and returns the result.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Responding to a Click with onclick
snippet: The onclick attribute names a function to call when the button is clicked, and the function must be defined inside a script tag.

subject: mad2
title: 6. Reading and Writing the Text Box
snippet: document.getElementById gives an element whose value attribute can be read and then replaced by the answer.

subject: mad2
title: 7. Validation and try-catch
snippet: Check that the expression is not empty, and wrap the evaluation in try and catch so a bad expression does not break the page.

subject: mad2
title: 8. Logging Results by Creating DOM Nodes
snippet: createElement and createTextNode build list items dynamically, and appendChild adds them to the existing page.

subject: mad2
title: 9. Scientific Functions with math.js
snippet: Including math.js and calling math.evaluate instead of eval gives scientific functions such as sin.

subject: mad2
title: 10. addEventListener and onload
snippet: Attaching the click handler in an initialize function, called from the body onload event, keeps the HTML free of JavaScript.

subject: mad2
title: 11. What Was Learned and What Comes Next
snippet: The screencast covered dynamic node creation, event handling, exception handling and functions, and the next part adds a grid of buttons.

subject: mad2
title: JavaScript Collections - Iterations and Destructuring
snippet: Covers iterating arrays and objects with for, for-in and for-of, why objects are not directly iterable, Object.entries, arrays with holes, the spread operator, the higher-order array methods find, filter, map, reduce and sort, and destructuring of arrays and objects including the rest pattern.

subject: mad2
title: 1. The C-style for Loop with let
snippet: A for loop that increments its index looks like C and needs the index declared with let.

subject: mad2
title: 2. for-in over an Array
snippet: for-in gives the indices of defined elements, skips holes, and works with const because each pass gets a new block scope.

subject: mad2
title: 3. for-of over an Array
snippet: for-of gives the values themselves, including undefined ones, so no indexing is needed.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Iterating an Object
snippet: for-in over an object gives its keys, but for-of fails because an object is not iterable.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Object.entries
snippet: Object.entries turns an object into an iterable list of key and value pairs.

subject: mad2
title: 6. new Array(5) and Holes
snippet: An array created with new Array is full of holes that read as undefined, and for-in skips them.

subject: mad2
title: 7. The Spread Operator
snippet: Three dots before an array spread its elements into the surrounding array instead of nesting it.

subject: mad2
title: 8. find and filter
snippet: find returns the first element for which a function is true, and filter returns all such elements.

subject: mad2
title: 9. map
snippet: map applies a function to every element and returns the new values.

subject: mad2
title: 10. reduce
snippet: reduce combines all elements into one value using a callback and an initial accumulator.

subject: mad2
title: 11. sort
snippet: The default sort is lexical, so numbers need a comparator function.

subject: mad2
title: 12. Array Destructuring
snippet: Destructuring assigns the first elements of an array to variables and ignores the rest.

subject: mad2
title: 13. Object Destructuring and Rest
snippet: Destructuring pulls named keys out of an object, with optional renaming and a rest object for the remaining keys.

subject: mad2
title: Screencast 2.2 - JavaScript - GUI Calculator
snippet: Extends the basic calculator into a keypad-style GUI calculator using Bootstrap grid rows of buttons, moves the log to its own row, colours operator buttons, uses the equals button for evaluation, and adds inputNumber and inputOperator functions that append to the expression box, then lists exercises to finish the calculator.

subject: mad2
title: 1. Goal and Plan
snippet: Build a calculator that looks like the operating system's built-in one, finish about 60 percent, and leave the rest as an exercise.

subject: mad2
title: 2. Keypad Rows with the Grid
snippet: Each keypad row is a Bootstrap row of four columns holding one button each, under a row with the text box.

subject: mad2
title: 3. Moving the Log to the Last Row
snippet: The log gets its own final row so it appears below the keypad.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Button Labels and Colours
snippet: Number and operator buttons get their labels, and operator buttons use a different Bootstrap colour class.

subject: mad2
title: 5. The Equals Button
snippet: Giving the equals button the id calculate reuses the existing click handler, so the Calculate button is no longer needed.

subject: mad2
title: 6. inputNumber
snippet: inputNumber appends a digit to the text box by string concatenation.

subject: mad2
title: 7. inputOperator
snippet: inputOperator works the same way, appending an operator, so 7, /, 8 and equals give 0.875.

subject: mad2
title: 8. Suggested Improvements (Exercises)
snippet: Add clear and backspace, a decimal point, better layout, centralised listeners, and extra functions such as square and brackets.

subject: mad2
title: JavaScript - Modularity and Objects
snippet: Explains why JavaScript needs modules, the history from plain scripts through CommonJS and AMD to ES6 modules, npm and bundlers, then covers import and export forms (named, renamed, default), read-only imported variables, and an introduction to JavaScript objects: object literals, methods, this, prototype-based inheritance, classes, and the difference between copying a reference and copying an object.

subject: mad2
title: 1. What a Module Is
snippet: A module bundles related functions, objects or values into a file that other code can import for reuse.

subject: mad2
title: 2. Front End versus Back End Loading
snippet: Browsers must decide where code comes from and cannot block, while Node on the server uses files and directories like Python.

subject: mad2
title: 3. History: Scripts, CommonJS, AMD, ES6 Modules
snippet: ES6 modules are the modern standard for both browsers and servers, with asynchronous loading, and are what this course uses.

subject: mad2
title: 4. npm and Bundlers
snippet: npm packages Node modules, and bundlers such as webpack and rollup turn them into files a browser can include; the course ignores this for now.

subject: mad2
title: 5. The script Tag with type module
snippet: A page needs type module on its script tag to use import and export, and imported files are loaded automatically.

subject: mad2
title: 6. Basic Import and Export
snippet: A value marked export in one file can be imported by name into another.

subject: mad2
title: 7. Named Exports and the Missing-Export Error
snippet: Only items marked for export can be imported; importing anything else is an error.

subject: mad2
title: 8. Renaming Imports and Exports
snippet: Use as to rename a name on import, or to export an internal name under a different public name.

subject: mad2
title: 9. Default Export
snippet: A module can export one default item, which the importer names freely without braces.

subject: mad2
title: 10. Imported Variables Are Read-Only
snippet: An importer cannot assign to an imported variable, but can change it by calling an exported function from the same module.

subject: mad2
title: 11. Think Before Structuring Modules
snippet: Plan how code is structured before deciding what to export and import.

subject: mad2
title: 12. Objects in JavaScript
snippet: Everything in JavaScript is an object, with literals, methods, this, and standard methods such as keys, values and entries.

subject: mad2
title: 13. Prototype-Based Inheritance and Classes
snippet: Objects inherit by setting another object as their prototype, with single inheritance, and the class keyword gives cleaner syntax.

subject: mad2
title: 14. Methods and this
snippet: A function stored on an object is a method, and this refers to the object itself, like self in Python.

subject: mad2
title: 15. Copying Objects
snippet: Assigning an object copies only a reference; the spread operator copies the values, but only one level deep.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
snippet: Covers getter and setter derived properties, the function methods call, apply and bind (with closures), prototype-based inheritance using the dunder proto property, and the class syntax with constructors, new, extends and super, including a small Animal, Dog and Cat hierarchy.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 1. Getters and Setters (Derived Properties)
snippet: The get and set keywords define derived properties so a computed value can be read and assigned like a plain property.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 2. The call Method
snippet: Every function has a call method whose first argument supplies this, so a method can run in the context of any object.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 3. The apply Method
snippet: apply works like call but takes its arguments as a single array, and extra arguments are ignored.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 4. The bind Method and Closures
snippet: bind creates a new function with this and some arguments fixed in advance.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 5. Inheritance with a Prototype
snippet: Setting the prototype of an object to another object gives it all of that object's properties and methods.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 6. Class Syntax over Prototypes
snippet: The class keyword is cleaner syntax for the same prototype-based inheritance, and is the recommended style.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 7. Constructor and new
snippet: A class has a constructor that sets up each object, and new creates an instance.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 8. extends and super
snippet: A subclass extends a parent class and calls super in its constructor to run the parent constructor.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: JavaScript - Function Methods, Prototypes and Classes
title: 9. Why Use Classes: Hierarchies
snippet: Classes let you build a hierarchy of related types, as in any object-oriented language.

subject: mad2
title: JavaScript - Asynchrony
snippet: Explains asynchrony in JavaScript: function calls as branches, stack frames and the call stack, the task queue and event loop, run-to-completion semantics and why blocking freezes a page, callbacks for long-running work, and Node.js examples contrasting synchronous and asynchronous file reading, with a pointer to promises and async/await.

subject: mad2
title: 1. What Asynchrony Means
snippet: Asynchrony means tasks can happen without a direct time relationship or tight synchronisation between them.

subject: mad2
title: 2. A Function Call Is a Branch
snippet: A function call is a branch to code stored elsewhere, with the added ability to come back.

subject: mad2
title: 3. Stack Frames and the Call Stack
snippet: The runtime saves the program counter and registers in a stack frame pushed on a call stack for each call.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Call Stack Example: main, f, g, h
snippet: Nested calls push frames and returns pop them in reverse order.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Task Queue and Event Loop
snippet: The event loop moves the next task from the queue onto the call stack only when the stack is empty.

subject: mad2
title: 6. Where Tasks Come From
snippet: Tasks come from events such as clicks, typing and network responses, which let the runtime avoid freezing.

subject: mad2
title: 7. Run-to-Completion
snippet: A task on the call stack must finish before the next is fetched, so a long task blocks everything.

subject: mad2
title: 8. The Blocking Demo
snippet: A loop that spins for five seconds makes the page unresponsive until it finishes.

subject: mad2
title: 9. Callbacks
snippet: A callback is a function you give to a long-running or network operation to be called when it completes.

subject: mad2
title: 10. Threads versus the Event Loop
snippet: JavaScript is single threaded but handles many requests by making input and output asynchronous.

subject: mad2
title: 11. Synchronous File Read in Node.js
snippet: readFileSync blocks everything until the file is read, which may be acceptable on a back end.

subject: mad2
title: 12. Asynchronous File Read with a Callback
snippet: readFile takes an anonymous callback with error and data parameters that runs after the read completes.

subject: mad2
title: 13. Summary, Promises and async/await
snippet: JavaScript pushes long-running work into separate tasks to stay responsive, and promises with async and await make this look like regular code.

subject: mad2
title: JavaScript: The JSON API
snippet: Introduces JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) as a frozen, text-based format for moving objects between programs, and the global JSON object with its stringify and parse methods. Demonstrates a Cat/Animal round trip and why a static fromJSON method is needed to rebuild a real Cat object from a parsed string.

subject: mad2
title: 1. What is JSON?
snippet: JSON is a text representation of an object that lets us move objects from one place to another; its specification is frozen.

subject: mad2
title: 2. The JSON API: stringify and parse
snippet: A global JSON object gives two main methods: JSON.stringify turns an object into a string, and JSON.parse turns a string back into a plain object.

subject: mad2
title: 3. Why is it called stringify?
snippet: The goal is a string that can be sent over a network, not necessarily written to a file.

subject: mad2
title: 4. Stringify demo on the Cat example
snippet: Stringifying a Cat gives a standardised, compact string with quoted names and values and no extra white space.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Getting back to an object
snippet: The JSON string carries no class information, so JSON.parse alone gives only a plain object, not a Cat.

subject: mad2
title: 6. The static fromJSON method
snippet: A class-level static method fromJSON builds a new object of the right class from a parsed JSON object.

subject: mad2
title: 7. JSON beyond JavaScript
snippet: JSON began in JavaScript but is used widely as a generic, easy-to-read data format.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
snippet: Introduces the frontend (UI and UX), what we want from it, imperative vs declarative programming, and the idea that UI = f(state). Separates system, application and ephemeral state, and shows how stateless HTTP forces a choice about where state lives. Four Tic-Tac-Toe implementations (Flask with server state, vanilla JavaScript with client state, basic Vue, composed Vue components) motivate Vue.js, reactivity and computed properties. Ends with a long Q&A.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 1. Frontend, UI and UX
snippet: The frontend is the user-facing part of an app; a good UI is an effective one, not necessarily a fancy one.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 2. Frontend requirements and desirable aspects
snippet: Keep logic and data on the server; the frontend should look good, react quickly and adapt to different screens.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 3. Imperative vs declarative programming
snippet: Imperative code gives the steps; declarative code states the result you want and lets a system work out how.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 4. State and UI = f(state)
snippet: State is the memory of the system; given the state, the user interface is uniquely determined.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 5. System, application and UI (ephemeral) state
snippet: System state is everything stored; application state is what one user sees; UI state is short-lived display detail.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 6. Keeping state over stateless HTTP
snippet: HTTP is stateless, so state must live either mostly in the client or mostly on the server; real apps sit in between.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 7. Problem statement: Tic-Tac-Toe and why Vue.js
snippet: A simple game is implemented four ways to show where state lives and to motivate Vue.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 8. Q&A: UI design, load time, bandwidth and scripts
snippet: There is no single rule for layout or performance; judge by the real experience of your users.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 9. Q&A: why not use stateful protocols everywhere?
snippet: Connections break often, and stateful protocols cannot cope cheaply with that.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 10. Demo 1: Tic-Tac-Toe with Flask (server-side state)
snippet: All state is in global variables on the server; the client is just a set of links.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 11. Demo 2: Tic-Tac-Toe with vanilla JavaScript (client-side state)
snippet: State lives in the browser and the page is updated imperatively; reloading loses the state.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 12. Q&A: asynchronous JavaScript
snippet: Asynchronous behaviour was in JavaScript from the start; background data fetching became popular around 2004.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 13. Demo 3: basic Vue (reactivity and computed properties)
snippet: Vue watches data and recomputes dependent values and the page automatically.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 14. Demo 4: composed components in idiomatic Vue
snippet: A self-contained board component can be reused any number of times, each copy with its own state.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 15. Q&A: Vue basics
snippet: Vue is a JavaScript library that hides the repetitive work of tracking changes and redrawing the page.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: Frontend Implementation: State, Declarative UI and Vue.js
title: 16. Q&A: component state, server state and two-way binding
snippet: Each component instance has its own data; v-model binds in both directions.

subject: mad2
title: Screencast 3.1: Introduction to Vue.js
snippet: A hands-on screencast that builds a Hello World page into a small Vue 2 app. Sets up the editor, browser and Vue Devtools, includes Vue with a script tag, creates a Vue instance with el and data, and shows reactivity in Devtools. Then adds a button with v-on and methods, conditionals with v-if, v-else-if and v-else, two-way binding with v-model, an array of visitors, v-for loops and a computed count.

subject: mad2
title: 1. Setup: editor, browser and Vue Devtools
snippet: You need an editor, Firefox or Chrome, and the Vue Devtools add-on, which adds a Vue tab to the developer tools.

subject: mad2
title: 2. A plain Hello World page
snippet: Start with a simple HTML page and move the app code into a separate application.js file.

subject: mad2
title: 3. Plain JavaScript vs Vue, and which Vue
snippet: Setting innerHTML by hand does not scale to a full app, so we use Vue 2 (development build while learning).

subject: mad2
title: 4. The Vue instance: el, data and an expression
snippet: A Vue instance attaches to an element with el, holds its values in data, and the HTML shows them with an expression.

subject: mad2
title: 5. Vue Devtools and reactivity
snippet: Change a data value and the page updates by itself; you never touch the UI.

subject: mad2
title: 6. Events: v-on and methods
snippet: v-on plus an event name (such as click) calls a function defined under methods on the Vue object.

subject: mad2
title: 7. Counting replies with data
snippet: Add a count value to data, increase it inside the method and show it in the page.

subject: mad2
title: 8. Conditionals: v-if, v-else-if and v-else
snippet: Show different elements depending on the value of an attribute.

subject: mad2
title: 9. Taking input with v-model (two-way binding)
snippet: v-model binds an input and a data value in both directions.

subject: mad2
title: 10. Storing visitors in an array
snippet: Push each name into a visitors array and clear the input so the user sees it was used.

subject: mad2
title: 11. Looping with v-for
snippet: v-for repeats an element once for each item in an array.

subject: mad2
title: 12. Computed properties
snippet: A computed attribute is calculated from other data (here the length of visitors), so values never go out of sync.

subject: mad2
title: 13. Recap
snippet: The Vue object, data, v-on, v-model, conditionals and loops make up the basics of Vue.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
title: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
snippet: Details backend architectural principles for building scalable RESTful web APIs, semantic resource URI conventions, HTTP status code taxonomy (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx), idempotent vs non-idempotent operations, and structuring Flask-RESTful and FastAPI resource endpoints.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
title: 1. RESTful Architectural Constraints & URI Design
snippet: REST models systems as collections of resources identified by plural nouns (/api/v1/students), using standard HTTP verbs for operations.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
title: 2. HTTP Methods, Idempotency, and Safety
snippet: Safe methods (GET) do not modify server state; idempotent methods (PUT, DELETE) produce identical server states upon repetition.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
title: 3. Semantic HTTP Status Codes Taxonomy
snippet: Returning precise status codes (201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict) creates predictable API contracts.

subject: mad2
lectureTitle: RESTful Web Services: Resource URIs, HTTP Verbs, and API Design
title: 4. Resource-Based Routing in FastAPI & Flask-RESTful
snippet: FastAPI path operations map HTTP methods cleanly to Python functions with automatic query, path, and header parsing.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
title: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
snippet: Explores enterprise data architecture, the formal relational model vs document stores, transactional integrity guarantees (ACID), domain constraints, foreign key referential cascades, and business data flow patterns.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
title: 1. Data as an Enterprise Asset & OLTP vs OLAP
snippet: Modern businesses separate high-throughput operational transaction recording (OLTP) from historical multi-dimensional analytical processing (OLAP).

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
title: 2. The Formal Relational Model & Codd's Rules
snippet: A relation is a mathematical set of tuples over attribute domains, governed by predicate logic rather than physical storage offsets.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
title: 3. Integrity Constraints: Entity, Referential, & Domain
snippet: Integrity constraints enforce business domain rules at the database engine tier, preventing corrupt data states regardless of application bugs.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Foundations of Relational Data Systems & Business Integrity Constraints
title: 4. The ACID Framework in Enterprise Transactions
snippet: ACID properties ensure financial and logistical transactions complete reliably or abort entirely without leaving phantom states.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
snippet: Recaps scarcity and micro vs macroeconomics, then classifies economies as command, free market or mixed, and as open or closed. Explains why economics is a social science, shows economics as a study of a system (toothbrush case) with production, distribution and consumption, and a fuel allocation case. Introduces optimization with an objective function and constraints, worked through Ramu's tea and coffee stall and an organic farm, with the PPF idea. Ends with the central problems of an economy, markets, production, factors of production and the five economic sectors.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 1. Recap of basic concepts
snippet: Scarcity, the definition of economics and the micro/macro split set up why BDM focuses on macroeconomics for policy and microeconomics for firm problems.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 2. Economic systems: three types
snippet: An economy is classified by who takes the decisions: the government, the owners, or both.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 3. Command economy: how it works
snippet: In a command economy a central authority sets rules for what, for whom, when and how much to produce.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 4. Command economy: Q&A, examples and drawbacks
snippet: Command economies give tight control but are rigid, brittle and weak on motivation and innovation.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 5. Free market (capitalist) economy
snippet: In a free market economy companies and individuals take the decisions, with little or no government role.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 6. Mixed economy
snippet: A mixed economy is a free market with government restrictions in selected areas, such as social welfare, safety and customer trust.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 7. Summary of the three economic systems
snippet: Command is 100 percent government control, free is 100 percent owner control, mixed combines both.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 8. Open vs closed economy
snippet: An open economy exchanges trade, technology and investment with others; a closed economy keeps everything inside its boundary.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 9. Closed economy: advantages and disadvantages (Q&A)
snippet: A closed economy keeps technology secret but must develop everything from scratch, slowly and expensively.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 10. Why economics is a social science
snippet: Results in economics vary with place and people, unlike deterministic science, though economics uses optimization, a pure science tool.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 11. Economics as a system: the toothbrush case
snippet: Customer demand creates innovation; economics studies, analyzes and optimizes a system, which gives models.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 12. Production, distribution and consumption
snippet: Economics is the study of the production-to-consumption chain, optimizing limited resources against demand.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 13. Case study: fuel supply in Tier-1 vs Tier-3 cities
snippet: Limited fuel was allocated first to Tier-1 production centres, where there are no alternatives.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 14. Optimization: objective function and constraints
snippet: To optimize you need an objective function and constraints.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 15. Case study 1: Ramu's tea and coffee stall
snippet: Fix the budget constraint, then allocate what remains to find quantities and profit.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 16. The PPF idea and the Ramu Q&A
snippet: On the curve means full use of resources, under it means waste, beyond it needs extra resources.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 17. Case study 2: organic farming (Basmati rice and wheat)
snippet: A water limit and a minimum Basmati area decide how much wheat can be grown and what the profit is.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 18. Central problems of an economy
snippet: Every new firm must answer what, how and for whom to produce.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 19. Market and production: goods and services
snippet: A market is where commodities are exchanged; production turns raw materials into usable goods (visible) and services (invisible).

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 20. Factors of production
snippet: Land, labor, physical capital and entrepreneurship are needed for every production activity.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 21. The five economic sectors
snippet: Economic activity is split into primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary and quinary sectors.

subject: bdm
lectureTitle: Fundamentals of Economics: Economic Systems, Optimization and Production
title: 22. Q&A: dominance of the tertiary sector
snippet: Depending heavily on services raises dependence on others and competition, so a balanced mix of sectors is needed.
